 Hong Kong Is Your Halloween Playground This October, And The Dress Code Is Cosplay
 From anime-inspired street parties and haunted red minibuses to immersive horror experiences and costume-friendly tram rides, Hong Kong is giving Halloween a distinctly local twist.
 29 Oct 2026 | Team ELLE What if Halloween were less about finding the right party and more about dressing up and taking over an entire city? This October, Hong Kong is making a case for exactly that, with its streets, nightlife districts and cultural hotspots transforming into a playground for cosplay enthusiasts, pop-culture fans and anyone looking for an excuse to go all out with their Halloween wardrobe. 
 Across five participating districts, Central, Kai Tak, Lan Kwai Fong, Mong Kok and Tsim Sha Tsui East, the celebrations bring together themed street parties, cosplay experiences, electronic music, immersive installations and distinctly Hong Kong references. With festivities culminating on Halloween night, 31 October, the city offers plenty of ways to experience the spooky season, one costume at a time. 
 The theme is simple: make the streets your runway. From neon-lit installations and DJ parties to character-inspired celebrations and interactive photo spots, Hong Kong is turning Halloween into an opportunity to step outside your usual wardrobe and into an entirely different character. 
 Kai Tak Sports Park 
 Five Neighbourhoods, Five Ways To Celebrate Halloween 
 If your idea of Halloween involves a little spectacle, start in Central. The district brings art, culture and the spooky season together through large-scale installations at Statue Square Gardens and themed activities along Chater Road. Giant eyeballs, a mysterious gateway and a haunted jail create striking photo opportunities, while outdoor music parties, family carnivals and cosplay celebrations add to the festivities. It is a chance to explore the city's cultural heart with a Halloween twist. 
 At Kai Tak Sports Park, the mood shifts towards music, dance and community. Neon installations, street dance performances and a DJ party soundtracked by Cantopop classics set the scene, while a marketplace offers Halloween-inspired finds. Local comic artists contribute three-dimensional photo spots, and a dedicated pet photo zone means your four-legged companion can join the dress-up plans. On Halloween itself, trick-or-treat activities, treasure hunts and professional body painting add to the carnival atmosphere. 
 Halloween Cosplay Party at Lan Kwai Fong  
 For those who prefer their Halloween with a side of nightlife, Lan Kwai Fong brings its signature party energy to the celebrations. The district's programme features themed evenings such as 'Monster DJ Night', 'Wizard Block Party' and 'Monsters Night', with cosplayers, live street broadcasts, photo installations and DJ performances taking over its streets and alleyways. Whether you arrive as your favourite fictional character or coordinate an elaborate group costume with friends, this is where dressing up becomes part of the night out. 
 Mong Kok gives the festivities a distinctly local personality. At Langham Place's Halloween street festival, the city's iconic red minibus gets a monstrous makeover in the form of the 'Mong Kok Haunted Minibus', a giant installation by designer-toy artist DANSIN. The programme also brings together champion cosplayers, local bands, DJs, street dancers and buskers. Between performances, visitors can sample Halloween-inspired Hong Kong delicacies, including egg waffles with inventive flavours, themed snacks and limited-edition desserts. 
 Over in Tsim Sha Tsui East, electronic music and cosplay meet against a backdrop of neon installations and Victoria Harbour views. Themed celebrations invite visitors to dress as anime and gaming characters before turning to iconic film characters, with the festivities culminating in a 'Grand Halloween Gala' on 31 October. Food stalls, costume booths and face-painting experiences round out the programme, offering another way to make a night exploring the city feel distinctly Halloween-coded. 
 From Disney Villains To Immersive Horror 
 Beyond the street celebrations, Hong Kong's two major theme parks bring their own interpretations of Halloween to the city. 
 At Hong Kong Disneyland Resort, Disney Halloween Time runs until 1 November, inviting guests to unleash their wicked side as Disney Villains take over the park. The programme features Halloween-themed entertainment, villain encounters, musical performances, themed dining experiences and trick-or-treat fun. Guests can also embrace the occasion with matching looks among friends and family, making it an opportunity to dress up and lean into their favourite Disney characters. From villain-led festivities to appearances by notorious Disney Villains throughout the day, the celebration invites visitors to party like a villain from daylight to moonlight. 
 'Cheers Fiesta' Returns, with Halloween Ambassadors Treating Guests to Free Drinks 
 For a more horror-led experience, Ocean Park Hong Kong's Halloween Fest also runs until 1 November. This year's edition partners with 'Under the Castle', the original fantasy intellectual property created and creatively directed by global music and style icon Jackson Wang. At The Summit, a mysterious ancient castle rises from the mist, drawing visitors into shadowy halls and a gloomy nightmare-scape that blends gothic aesthetics with immersive storytelling. The experience extends beyond the scares, with themed food and beverage offerings, game booths and exclusive merchandise. For anyone who prefers their Halloween atmosphere dark, dramatic and a little unsettling, this is one to add to the itinerary. 
 The Most Unexpected Way To Get Around? In Costume 
 One of the more playful additions to Hong Kong's Halloween celebrations is the chance to take the party on the move. Special Halloween-themed open-top sightseeing buses and 'Ding Ding' trams operate on selected dates in October, including 30 and 31 October, giving eligible visitors another way to experience the city in costume. 
 Both locals and visitors dressed in Halloween costumes who meet the designated spending requirements at participating merchants can redeem complimentary ride tickets at designated redemption points. Participating properties include Hongkong Land, Kai Tak Sports Park, Langham Place and Sino Group locations, including Tsim Sha Tsui Centre, Empire Centre and China Hong Kong City. 
 Halloween Cosplay Party at Lan Kwai Fong 
 The open-top sightseeing bus connects major festive hotspots across Hong Kong Island and Kowloon, while specially themed Hong Kong Tramways vehicles offer another way to take in the city's streets. With the final scheduled rides coinciding with Halloween Eve and Halloween Day, the experience gives costume enthusiasts an opportunity to make the journey part of the celebration. 
 Just remember to check the designated redemption points, minimum spending requirements, ride schedules and applicable terms before setting out. Even the most committed cosplayer needs a little logistical planning. 
 Where To Shop For Your Halloween Alter Ego 
 A citywide cosplay celebration calls for a little wardrobe preparation. Fortunately, Hong Kong's street markets offer plenty of opportunities to find a look without committing to an elaborate costume budget. 
 In Central, Pottinger Street is a convenient stop for anyone hunting for costume accessories before heading towards Lan Kwai Fong. For more options, Tai Yuen Street in Wan Chai and Fuk Wing Street in Sham Shui Po are known for their selection of character outfits, playful accessories and costume-related finds. 
 From classic ghosts and witches to anime favourites, gaming characters and pop-culture icons, the possibilities are wide open. Whether you're planning a full transformation, recreating a favourite film character or simply adding a dramatic accessory to your going-out look, the aim is to have fun with the process. After all, Halloween is one of the few occasions when the more committed the outfit, the better. 
 Halloween Cosplay Party at Lan Kwai Fong 
 With five participating districts, two major theme parks, costume-friendly transport and markets filled with potential outfit upgrades, Hong Kong offers plenty of ways to make the final days of October memorable. Come for the cosplay, stay for the pop-culture spectacle, and consider this your invitation to make Halloween a little more elaborate this year. 
 Planning your visit: The Halloween celebrations culminate on 31 October 2026, while Disney Halloween Time at Hong Kong Disneyland Resort and Halloween Fest at Ocean Park Hong Kong run until 1 November. The Halloween Sightseeing Bus and Party Tram experiences are scheduled for 30 and 31 October, with complimentary rides subject to costume and spending requirements at participating merchants.
